text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Mortgage lenders estimate that they made over 200 billion crowns in new loans in 1996, compared to 139 bilion in 1995.
--The European beef scare of 1996 pushed farm-gate pork prices to an average 11.35 crowns per kilo from 10.39 the year before.
--A new Sonar poll shows export businesses optimistic about 1997.
--Another Sonar survey shows most respondents believe that unemployment will fall next year.
--The most profitable shares in 1996 were not those on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange's KFX top 20 index but those lying just below the top 20.
--Bang & Olufsen's fast-growing telecom division is developing its own digital cordless phone.
